note_on_method: Three of the five filter slugs have a lawful data driver in Boulder. Free does, because the City prices every outdoor court in one sentence: "Courts are first come and free to all park visitors". Outdoor does, because the City's court table sits under the heading "Outdoor court layout and location" and its drop-in schedule says "outdoor courts" in words. Indoor does, because the City counts "3 indoor courts" in each recreation centre gymnasium on its pickleball page. Lights has no driver: "Lights are not guaranteed for use of courts after sunset" is a rule rather than a per-venue answer, and no venue carries one.

slots.why_this_filter:
Every verified pickleball court in Boulder is free to walk onto, so this page holds the same five venues as the city page: North Boulder Recreation Center, East Boulder Community Center, South Boulder Recreation Center, Chautauqua Park and Foothills Community Park, twenty outdoor courts between them. The City says so in one sentence on its Racket Sports page, "Courts are first come and free to all park visitors, a reserved court is available to secure your date and time", and again in its FAQ, where unreserved courts "remain free to use on a first-come, first-play basis". Most parks departments never think to write it down; Boulder did. It is one of seven cities on this site with a verified free court, and, with Cape Coral, one of only two where every published venue is free.

Free has two edges here, and the City states both. Free is the walk-up price; a reservation, which the City calls "exclusive use" of a court, costs $10 an hour, doubled from $5 on November 14, 2025. And free applies to the outdoor courts. The nine indoor courts are "included with your daily entry fee or pass", so an indoor session costs whatever the door costs, a figure the City does not print on the pages read.
slots.what_qualifies:
A venue appears here when the City of Boulder states that playing on it costs nothing, and all five published venues qualify under the same sentence. It sits under "Outdoor Court Reservations" on the Racket Sports page and covers every row of the court table beneath it. At the two parks, Chautauqua and Foothills, that is the whole of the price. At the three recreation centres it is the price of the outdoor courts, and the City draws the indoor line itself: "To play indoor drop-in pickleball, recreation center daily admission fee or membership is required."

What does not qualify is a court you have reserved: $10 an hour per court, one per person per day, two hours at most, with no refunds for weather. At Foothills that distinction matters more than elsewhere, because a court not reserved between 7 a.m. and noon "is designated as inline hockey court".

faqs.a: $10 an hour per court, for tennis and pickleball alike, since November 14, 2025, when the fee doubled from $5 and reservations stopped being included in recreation memberships. One reservation per person per day, two hours at most.
Not on their own. Indoor drop-in is "included with your daily entry fee or pass" at the three recreation centres, so the price is the door. The City does not print that fee on the pages read.

slots.why_this_filter:
Twenty of Boulder's twenty-nine verified courts are outdoors, at all five published venues, and the City states it plainly: the table that counts them sits under a heading that reads "Outdoor court layout and location", and the drop-in schedule says "outdoor courts" in words.

Outdoor means something specific here. "Pickleball play is on tennis courts with pickleball lines", the City says, "Except for Foothills Community Park which is a designated inline hockey rink." Sixteen of the twenty are lines on tennis courts: four at North Boulder, eight at South Boulder, two at East Boulder and two at Chautauqua. The nets column of the table reads "Rolling" on every row, with the rule that "Pickleball nets should be rolled off tennis courts after completion of play and when not in use". The other four are on a rink, mornings only, bring your own net.

The outdoor courts are where the free sentence lives, where the reservation system runs, and where the City's two scheduled sessions happen: daily mornings at South Boulder on six courts, and Tuesday and Thursday mornings plus Wednesday and Friday evenings at North Boulder on four. The City does not say whether any of them are lit, or what they are surfaced with.
slots.what_qualifies:
A venue appears here when the City of Boulder's court table lists it under "Outdoor court layout and location" with a pickleball count. Five qualify: South Boulder Recreation Center with eight, North Boulder Recreation Center with four, Foothills Community Park with four, East Boulder Community Center with two and Chautauqua Park with two.

Foothills qualifies on four courts that are pickleball courts from 7 a.m. to noon; outside that window the rink "is designated as inline hockey court". The nine indoor courts at the three recreation centres do not qualify for this page; each centre carries a count on both sides of the line. Tom Watson Park is not here because its only figure, 4, is under "Additional Tennis Courts". East Boulder Community Park is not here because the City states no count for it at all.

faqs.q: Which outdoor courts in Boulder have lights?
faqs.a: The City does not say, for any venue. Its one sentence on the subject is "Lights are not guaranteed for use of courts after sunset", so every venue here is recorded as unverified and Boulder has no lights page.

faqs.q: Do I need to bring a net?
faqs.a: At Foothills, yes: "Nets are not available onsite." Elsewhere the table's nets column reads "Rolling" and the City asks that nets be rolled off tennis courts after play, without saying in words whether one is provided.

faqs.q: Why does South Boulder say eight courts and six courts?
faqs.a: The City's table lists "8 pickleball"; its drop-in line sets aside "6 outdoor courts" for the morning session. Eight is the inventory and six is the morning allocation, and both figures are printed on the venue page.

slots.why_this_filter:
Three Boulder venues hold indoor pickleball courts, nine between them, and the City counts every one of them in words: "3 indoor courts" at North Boulder Recreation Center, "3 indoor courts" at East Boulder Community Center and "3 indoor courts" at South Boulder Recreation Center, on its pickleball page.

What indoor means in Boulder is specific, and the City is exact about it. "Drop-in pickleball is offered inside our recreation center basketball gymnasiums. Indoor play is only available during the designated drop-in pickleball times, listed below, and pickleball nets are not available outside listed drop-in hours." So an indoor court here exists for a listed window and not otherwise: Monday, Wednesday and Friday mornings at North Boulder; Monday afternoon, Monday evening and Sunday afternoon at East Boulder; Sunday morning and Tuesday and Thursday afternoons at South Boulder, and nothing at South Boulder from June through October.

The price is the door: "Indoor drop-in pickleball is included with your daily entry fee or pass", and the City does not print that fee on the pages read. Boulder is one of the few operators on this site that publishes a written drop-in schedule for both its indoor and its outdoor courts, so the window is known before you go.
slots.what_qualifies:
A venue appears here when the City of Boulder's pickleball page counts indoor courts at it. Three qualify, with three courts each: North Boulder Recreation Center, whose line reads "Monday, Wednesday, Friday: 7:30 to 10:30 am on 3 indoor courts"; East Boulder Community Center, listed on that page as East Boulder Recreation Center; and South Boulder Recreation Center, which carries the City's asterisk, "There is no indoor Pickleball at South Boulder Recreation Center from June through October". South Boulder qualifies through the off-season because the count is stated and the closure is printed beside it.

What does not qualify is any court the City does not call indoor. Chautauqua Park and Foothills Community Park have no gymnasium and no indoor line. The "Two platform tennis courts with pickleball lines" the City offers for overflow at North Boulder are not counted at all.

faqs.a: They are "included with your daily entry fee or pass", so the price is the recreation centre's door charge, which the City does not print on the pages read. The outdoor courts at the same centres are free.

faqs.q: Is there indoor pickleball in summer?
faqs.a: Not at South Boulder: "There is no indoor Pickleball at South Boulder Recreation Center from June through October". North Boulder's and East Boulder's schedules carry no such note.

faqs.q: Which indoor venue has an evening session?
faqs.a: East Boulder Community Center, Monday 6 to 8 pm on three courts. It is the only evening indoor session the City prints. The other indoor windows are mornings and afternoons.
